contexts.text: At last they do not care whether they mix together profane with holy things... The things which have been mixed together by profanations adhere mixed together...

The reason why the new light or morning does not come until the Church has been vastated, is that the things of faith and charity have been mixed together with things profane; and, so long as they are mixed together, nothing of light or of charity can ever be insinuated; for the tares destroy all the good seed.
They who have the doctrine of faith... are able to mix together truths with falsities...
Being the Lord's, it is never to be mixed together with the things of man's will. Signified.
Not to eat the flesh in its soul, the blood = not to mix together profane with holy things. Explained.
The commingling of what is holy and of what is profane.
But goods are never so commingled with evils, or evils with goods, that they cannot be separated; for, if they were commingled, the man would perish to eternity... AC 2269:end. AC 2284:2.
The Lord constantly provides that evil be not commingled with good.
Goods and truths are profaned when commingled with falsities and evils.
He then commingles evils with goods, and falsities with truths, so that they cannot be separated. AC 6959:2.
This is the commingling of truth and falsity...
That this good must not be commingled with the good of another. Signified, Explained.
When the truth of faith which has once been acknowledged is afterwards applied to evil, it is commingled with the falsity from evil; whence is profanation.
That the worship of the Lord from the truths of the Church must not be commingled with falsities from evil. Signified, Explained.

Truths with the evil are not commingled with the falsities from evil with them so long as they are only in the memory... But if truths are falsified to favour evil... then they are commingled; whence is the profanation of truth.
A guard lest spiritual good and celestial good be commingled; thus the Middle and the Inmost Heaven. Signified, Explained.
He sprinkled it upon the faces of the waters = a commingling with truths... It is signified that falsity from infernal delight had been commingled with the truths which are from Heaven.
(Therefore) the Lord exquisitely separates good and evil, lest they should be commingled, with man...
He then commingles holy with profane things; which, when they have been commingled, cannot be separated otherwise than by the destruction of the whole.
The Lord separates evil and good so that the one is interior and the other exterior, and thus provides against their being commingled.
That he then commingles good and evil, insomuch that they cannot be separated. Explained.
This freedom with its rationality has been destroyed with those who have commingled good and evil in themselves...
Such is the lot with those who in this way commingle holy with profane things.

But when a man comes into the use of his rationality and freedom... if he then acknowledges truths and lives according to them, and afterwards denies them, he commingles holy with profane things... Whereas if a man is in evil from the time when he has become of his own rationality and freedom... and afterwards acknowledges the truths of faith and lives according to them, provided he then remains in them to the end of life, he does not commingle them...
This is the worst kind of profanation; for the reason that they commingle holy with profane things so that they cannot be separated...
With a hypocrite... the evil is within and the good is without; and so the two are... not commingled.
Many truths can be received by the understanding, and be stored up in the memory, and yet not be commingled with the evil of the will...

That if (the will were to receive truths) sooner and more, the will would adulterate good, and the understanding would falsify truth, by commingling them with evils and the derivative falsities. Explained.
(The lukewarm) have commingled truths with falsities, and goods with evils...
With them, the chaste is above, and the non-chaste beneath, and there is as it were a door on hinges interposed by the Lord... lest they mix themselves together.
What is more detestable than for a man to commingle his soul with the soul of a husband in his wife?
These things are not to be mixed up (that is, confounded).
They commingle holy with profane things.
Thus a commingling of ideas... The penalty. SE 2059 (Immixtae). SE 2067. SE 2073.
To commingle a spirit of perversities in the midst of her () = to pervert and falsify them.
Truths commingled with falsities are cast out. Signified.
When the interiors are evils and falsities, and the exteriors goods and truths, there is a commingling of both...

Good and evil, and the truth of good and the falsity of evil, are commingled when evil and falsity are in the spirit of man, but good and truth in his deeds and speech; for what is interior acts into what is exterior...
But the commingling of good and evil, and of truth and falsity, is not the profanation of good and truth. Explained.
Lamentation on account of the defect and commingling of truth with falsity. Signified.
That these delights will cease, is signified by all joy is mixed together ().
This disputation (about good and evil, and truth and falsity) is signified by I will commingle Egypt with Egypt... ().
